messages:
Elaine (Docs): Dropping a compact thread here — drafting a short 'archive + export manifest' section for the SOC2 audit-log docs. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4999 :wave:
Sam (Security): Nice. Two asks: 1) show a manifest example that accompanies exports (list of files + manifest_hash + export_timestamp + exported_by). 2) define provenance_hash semantics so auditors can verify integrity.
Elaine (Docs): Working on both. Proposed manifest example (in docs):
```json
{
  "files": ["tenant_acctX_20260301_part1.jsonl"],
  "export_timestamp": "2026-03-01T12:00:00Z",
  "exported_by": "ops@redwood.ai",
  "manifest_hash": "sha256:..."
}
```
Matt (SDK): Note: export endpoint streams JSONL; each record should include schema_version and provenance_hash. SDK will provide a tiny verifier helper to check provenance. I'll PR a helper in sdk/audit/utils by EOD.
Nijah (Legal): Wording suggestion: instead of "we keep" use precise language: "By default, Redwood retains and makes available audit evidence for export for 365 days; customers may configure retention per tenant where permitted by contract. Records subject to a legal hold are preserved until release and are exempt from standard TTL deletion." Approve with that phrasing.
Kai (PM): Customer question: if they shorten retention, can they bulk-export prior to deletion? We should mention export API and legal_hold endpoints as migration aids.
Elaine (Docs): I'll add a migration note: "When a tenant retention window is reduced, new TTLs apply only to subsequently written evidence. Customers should run a bulk export (or apply legal holds) before the effective date to preserve existing data. Use the export API to retrieve JSONL bundles and store them externally if long-term retention is required."
Sam (Security): Add a short caution: changes to redaction rules can alter exported content. Recommend including schema_version and provenance_hash in every exported record; provenance_hash = sha256(canonical_event + schema_version + export_timestamp).
Elaine (Docs): Good — will include that exact formula. Also adding curl + python examples.
Elaine (Docs): cURL export example:
```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/audit/export?tenant=acct_X&from=2026-01-01T00:00:00Z&to=2026-02-28T23:59:59Z" \
  -o acct_X_20260101-20260228.jsonl
```
Elaine (Docs): Python SDK example (streaming):
```python
from redwood.audit import AuditClient
client = AuditClient(api_key=os.getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY"))
with client.export_stream(tenant_id="acct_X", start="2026-01-01T00:00:00Z", end="2026-02-28T23:59:59Z") as stream:
    for line in stream:
        record = json.loads(line)
        # record includes schema_version, exported_by, export_timestamp, provenance_hash
        local_store.write(record)
```
Matt (SDK): I'll include a small script in the SDK repo that verifies manifest_hash and validates provenance_hash per-record; will link it from the docs.
Elaine (Docs): Found a bad anchor in docs/retention-archival.md (link currently points to #export-manifest-example but the section header is "Export manifest"). I'll fix the anchor in the PR. deploy-bot, can you add the linkfix to the checklist?
deploy-bot: Reminder: tiny PR checklist — include linkfix, add changelog entry, and add cross-link to SDK verification helper when available.
Nijah (Legal): One more minor edit: add "available for export" to the default retention sentence to clarify access. That aligns with contractual obligations.
Sam (Security): Approve technical phrasing. Suggest we include a short auditor note recommending storing exported bundles in customer-managed cold storage and signing manifests locally for independent verification.
Kai (PM): Timing: aim to ship in the next docs deploy. Elaine, put a changelog bullet and mark the PR ready once Matt posts the SDK helper link.
Elaine (Docs): Will update PR with revised wording, manifest + provenance explanation, curl/python snippets, and the linkfix. Thanks all! :tada:
